title: Boss: hashing
summary: Anagram checks, the longest run, word frequencies and an LRU cache.

steps.title: Anagram check
prompt: Write `bool IsAnagram(string a, string b)`: do the two strings use exactly the same characters, the same number of times? Case and spaces count as characters.
Do it in `O(n)` with **one** dictionary: count up for `a`, count down for `b`, and check every count ends at zero. No sorting.
solution: foreach (var c in a) counts[c] = counts.GetValueOrDefault(c) + 1;
foreach (var c in b) counts[c] = counts.GetValueOrDefault(c) - 1;
template: Dojo.Eq("aab / abb (same letters, different counts)", false, IsAnagram("aab", "abb"));
hints: Different lengths can never be anagrams.
`+1` for each char of `a`, `-1` for each char of `b`, then `counts.Values.All(n => n == 0)`.

steps.title: Longest consecutive run
prompt: Write `int LongestRun(int[] a)`: the length of the longest sequence of **consecutive integers** found anywhere in the array, in any order.

Sorting would be `O(n log n)`; do it in `O(n)`. Put everything in a `HashSet`. A number `x` **starts** a run only if `x - 1` is not in the set; from each start, count upwards while `x + 1, x + 2, ...` are present. Each number is visited at most twice.
template: Dojo.Eq("an empty array gives 0", 0, LongestRun(new int[0]));
Dojo.Eq("duplicates do not count twice", 3, LongestRun(new[] { 1, 2, 2, 3 }));
for (var dojoI = 0; dojoI < dojoBig.Length; dojoI++) dojoBig[dojoI] = dojoI % 2 == 0 ? dojoI / 2 : 1_000_000 - dojoI;
Dojo.Eq("300,000 numbers finish in time", 150_000, LongestRun(dojoBig));
hints: `var set = new HashSet<int>(a);` then loop over the set (not the array) so duplicates are skipped.
Skip `x` when `set.Contains(x - 1)`. Otherwise count `length` while `set.Contains(x + length)`.

steps.title: Top words
prompt: Write `List<string> TopWords(string text, int k)`: the `k` most frequent words, most frequent first. Break ties **alphabetically**.
- Words are separated by single spaces; compare them in lower case.
- If there are fewer than `k` distinct words, return them all.
TopWords("the cat and the hat and the bat", 2)   // [the, and]
Count with a dictionary, then LINQ: `OrderByDescending(...).ThenBy(...).Take(k)`.
solution: return counts.OrderByDescending(p => p.Value).ThenBy(p => p.Key, StringComparer.Ordinal).Take(k).Select(p => p.Key).ToList();
template: Dojo.Eq("the example", new List<string> { "the", "and" }, TopWords("the cat and the hat and the bat", 2));
Dojo.Eq("ties break alphabetically", new List<string> { "bat", "cat", "hat" }, TopWords("the cat and the hat and the bat", 6).Skip(2).ToList());
Dojo.Eq("case is ignored", new List<string> { "go" }, TopWords("Go go GO stop", 1));
Dojo.Eq("fewer words than k", new List<string> { "a", "b" }, TopWords("b a", 5));
hints: Split with `StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries` so empty text gives no words.

steps.title: LRU cache
prompt: A **least-recently-used cache** holds at most `capacity` entries. When it is full and a new key arrives, it evicts the entry that was used longest ago.
- `int Get(int key)`: the value, or `-1` if missing. A hit counts as a **use**.
- `void Put(int key, int value)`: insert or update (an update is also a use); evict the least recently used entry if this pushes it over capacity.

Both must be `O(1)`. Combine a `LinkedList<(int Key, int Value)>` (most recent at the front) with a `Dictionary<int, LinkedListNode<(int Key, int Value)>>` that jumps straight to each node. `list.Remove(node)`, `list.AddFirst(node)` and `list.RemoveLast()` are all `O(1)`.
starter: private readonly LinkedList<(int Key, int Value)> order = new();
private readonly Dictionary<int, LinkedListNode<(int Key, int Value)>> nodes = new();
public void Put(int key, int value) { }
solution: private readonly LinkedList<(int Key, int Value)> order = new();
private readonly Dictionary<int, LinkedListNode<(int Key, int Value)>> nodes = new();
public void Put(int key, int value)
var node = new LinkedListNode<(int Key, int Value)>((key, value));
template: Dojo.Eq("2 was least recently used, so it was evicted", -1, dojoC.Get(2));
Dojo.Eq("1 survived because Get used it", 10, dojoC.Get(1));
Dojo.Eq("updating 1 counted as a use, so 3 went", -1, dojoC.Get(3));
for (var dojoI = 0; dojoI < 200_000; dojoI++) { dojoBig.Put(dojoI, dojoI); dojoBig.Get(dojoI / 2); }
hints: `Get`: look up the node; move it to the front with `order.Remove(node); order.AddFirst(node);`.
`Put`: remove any existing node, add a new node at the front, store it in `nodes`. If over capacity, remove `order.Last` from both structures.
